fields.description:
Outcome and context

Ops users need to see which Brand Ambassador (BA) owns each Sign-Up without opening the record and going to the More Info (Ops) tab. Emily asked on 2026-09-30 how to filter the full "All" Sign-Ups list to one BA's signups in split view, and said the BA tag needs to be "more prevalent" in the Ops view. She also asked that this go on the agenda for the same-day call. This ticket captures the visibility change. It is Ops-only by intent, and that still needs to be confirmed (see Open questions).

Current state

  • Brand Ambassador is a lookup field on Sign-Up. It sits on the More Info (Ops) tab, under General Information.

  • The split view list cards show Player, Operator, Status and Created time. The Sign-Up highlights panel shows Operator, Partner, Market Country, Market State, Vertical, Status, Proof Status and Completion. BA is on neither.

  • Split view does not support filtering or sorting. Users must filter in table view, then switch back to split view. The filter stays applied. Emily has this answer.

  • The BA filter value is a plain text box, not a picklist, because BA is a lookup field. Emily asked if it could be a picklist. Standard list view filters do not offer that for a lookup field.

  • Emily's column template lists 22 columns (Player through Notes) for the "All Sign-Ups" list view. It has two notes: freeze up to column G (Country), and "In the OPS View we need to see the BA Tag as well." The template does not say which columns are Ops-only.

  • Related work: WAGR-423 covers the Sign-Up list views ("All Active", sort order and column alignment). This ticket builds on those lists and should not start before the WAGR-423 column set is final.

Proposed solution

Options to review. None is decided yet.

  1. Add Brand Ambassador as a column on an Ops-only Sign-Up list view. In split view, only the first four list fields show on the cards, so BA must sit in the first four columns to appear there.

  2. Add Brand Ambassador to the Sign-Up highlights panel or compact layout for Ops. Compact layouts are assigned by record type, not by profile, so an Ops-only header needs a separate Lightning record page assigned to the Ops profile. The exact approach is not confirmed.

  3. Restrict the BA field with field-level security to Ops profiles or an Ops permission set. FLS is the reliable control. Sharing a list view with the Ops group only controls who sees that list view.

Acceptance criteria (draft, pending confirmation)

  1. An Ops user sees the Brand Ambassador name in the Ops Sign-Up list view without opening the record.

  2. Non-Ops users (BAs and Reps) do not see the BA column or field, if Ops-only is confirmed.

  3. Existing list views for other users are not changed.

  4. The change is checked in split view and in table view.

Open questions

  • Where should BA be more prominent: the list, the record header, or both? Emily was asked or will be asked on the call.

  • Should BA be Ops-only? Emily's template says BA is added "in the OPS View." It does not say BAs or Reps must not see it.

  • Which of Emily's 22 template columns are Ops-only? The template does not say.

  • Can Lightning freeze columns up to column G? Not confirmed. This is not a standard list view setting as far as we know.

  • Is a BA picklist filter needed? If yes, options are saved list views per BA, or custom work. Custom work is a separate ticket.

Out of scope

  • Freezing columns (until confirmed possible).

  • Building a BA picklist filter or a custom filter component.

  • The "All Active" list view, sort order and Recently Viewed alignment (WAGR-423).

Source

  • Emily Vandenberg, Slack thread in the WagerTech channel, 2026-09-30, 9:51 AM to 10:28 AM: https://jumpr-solutions.slack.com/archives/C0BBC05C2HG/p1790776304286699

  • Emily's column template (Table View - Column Template): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sljtqwg7PL7OeLT6HKvjnXW9EC-70v9t5wo74cCwgjo/edit?gid=0

  • Salesforce Ben, "Your Complete Guide to Salesforce Split View" (filter and sort only in table view): https://www.salesforceben.com/your-complete-guide-to-salesforce-split-view/

  • Related: WAGR-423, parent epic WAGR-305.

comments.body:
@Cedrick Infantado , quick check before I reply to Emily. She asked if the BA filter value in the Sign-Ups list view can be a picklist instead of a text box.

BA is a lookup, so I think the filter just gives a plain text box (type the name) and there's no dropdown option.

Is that right, or is there a way to get a dropdown that I'm missing? If not, I was going to offer saved list views per BA.

@Taryn Reithofer Yeah, you’re right. Since this is a lookup field, the only option is to have a text box in that filter.

How many BAs do they have? I’m worried that the list view would be too long.
@Cedrick Infantado Well not a lot looking at the test data but I’d have to ask what it would be in prod.
@Kobi Kunasekaran I learnt about this nifty filtering value! Where it points to the current user, but the thing is that BA’s don’t have table view edit access so they can’t point to themselves here.
But I guess this doesn’t make sense either way because Ops are searching for BA’s and not BA’s searching from themselves…
SORRY I’m feeling spammy I guess. I found some workarounds online but it would be a large lift. I’ll let Emily know and see what she says, perhaps it a V2 enhancement.

@Taryn Reithofer The $USER filter is something we will do as additional list views for only the lists Reps need to see. Once you finalize the columns, we’d basically clone and call it My New Signs Ups, My In Progress Sign Ups, etc. add the $USER filter to those. Those will be the list views Reps should have access to. Generally they shouldn’t have access to the all rep views, which we can control from the Sharing settings of those list views, we’ve left these open intentionally for now.

So if the underlying ask is that Reps should be able to easily see their assigned Sign Ups, we can do that without them needing to filter things manually.

If Ops wants an easy way to filter for specific reps with standard layouts, it’s unfortunately using the annoying filters. We can potentially make it a bit easier later through some hacks but it’ll require a small build + add some maintenance when new reps are added. This or we build reports if the point of what they need is for reporting and not necessarily for logging sign ups like reps.

## Outcome and context

When an Ops user searches a name in the top-level (global) search, the results should show enough detail to pick the right record without opening it. Emily asked on 2026-09-30 for two changes: (1) the Sign-Up results should show the same details as the Sign-Up table, and (2) the Accounts results should show the account type next to the name, so a Player, a Referrer and a BA can be told apart.

## Current state

* Emily's request came with a screenshot of the current search results. The screenshot could not be opened from Slack when this ticket was written, so the current columns are not yet documented here.
* The Sign-Up and Accounts result columns are not confirmed.
* Related: WAGR-483 covers the Accounts Recently Viewed list columns so record types are distinguishable. It is list view work, not search results.

## Proposed solution

Options to review. None is decided yet.

1. In Setup, open Object Manager > Sign-Up > Search Layouts > Search Results, and add the fields from the Sign-Up table to the results layout.
2. Do the same for Account, and add the account type (record type) to the results layout. If the record type cannot be added to the search results layout, review a formula field that shows the type.

Not confirmed: whether the Sign-Up table fields and the Account record type can all be added to a search results layout, and whether the global search dropdown (the quick results) uses the same layout as the full results page. Check both before promising this to Emily.

## Acceptance criteria (draft, pending confirmation)

1. A global search for a player name shows the agreed Sign-Up fields in the Sign-Up results.
2. The Accounts results show the account type (Player, Referrer, BA) next to the name.
3. No other object's search results or list views are changed.

## Open questions

* Which Sign-Up table fields does Emily want in the search results? The full column set, or a shortlist?
* Should the account type show for all users or Ops only?
* Do the changes apply to the search dropdown as well as the full results page?

## Out of scope

* Changes to list views (see WAGR-423 and WAGR-483).
* Ranking or matching logic for search.

## Source

* Emily Vandenberg, Slack, 2026-09-30, 10:54 AM ET: https://jumpr-solutions.slack.com/archives/C0BBC05C2HG/p1790780070785829

Summary

Set the final Deal Status value list once so lifecycle stories consume a single field definition.

Final values

Order

API value

Label

Meaning

1

Draft

Draft

Being set up; default; never sent to CMS.

2

Active

Active

Salesforce has activated/intends the Deal to be live. CMS Sync Status separately shows whether CMS accepted the latest state.

3

Paused

Paused

Temporary operational pause; lifecycle action hides/deactivates active Links and can later restore the pre-pause active set.

4

Inactive

Inactive

Automated informational state after inactivity threshold; does not deactivate Links or alter DRAs.

5

Closed

Closed

Longer-term locked state; reactivatable by permitted users.

6

Archived

Archived

Terminal; never normally reactivated; releases makeup.

Deactivate Review Required rather than delete it.

Requirements

  • Keep restricted picklist and field history.

  • Set Draft as default.

  • API values are exactly Draft, Active, Paused, Inactive, Closed, Archived.

  • Verify the actual deployed metadata uses Archived spelling.

  • Review Required is inactive and cannot be newly set through normal UI/API.

  • This story defines values only; behavior belongs to lifecycle action stories.

Important semantic clarification

  • Active does not mean CMS sync succeeded. Active may coexist with CMS Sync Status = Failed/Retrying.

  • Inactive is informational only. CMS must not interpret it as Pause/hide Links merely because the status value is Inactive.

Out of scope

  • Archive action/makeup release.

  • Closed locking/reactivation behavior.

  • Pause Link-state restoration.

  • CMS contract implementation.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Provide a controlled New Deal Screen Flow that creates a Deal in Draft with only the agreed setup fields, previews/validates the input, and can optionally hand off to the separate Commercial Terms flow after the Deal has committed.

## Deal Information

Required:

* Operator — lookup only; do not allow Operator creation.
* Partner — lookup only; do not allow Partner creation.
* Market Country.
* Vertical.
* Source.
* Deal Currency.
* Deal Effective Start Date.

Optional:

* Market State — blank means country-wide.
* Priority Tier.
* Notes.

## Defaults

* Deal Status = Draft from field default; do not expose Status as an input.
* Deal Currency:

    * United States → USD;
    * Canada → CAD;
    * otherwise org default;
    * apply only while Currency is blank; do not silently overwrite a user-selected Currency.
    
* Deal Effective Start Date defaults to today.
* Do not invent future-date activation/scheduling behavior.

## Independent business dimensions

Source and Partner are independent:

* Source = Direct describes how WagerTech sourced the Deal.
* Partner = Direct means no external Partner participates in that Deal.
* Never derive one from the other.

## Optional Commercial Terms handoff

Add checkbox: **Add Commercial Terms**.

If selected:

1. Create/commit the Deal first.
2. Launch the independent Add/Edit Commercial Terms Screen Flow.
3. Pass the new Deal Id.
4. A Commercial Terms error must not roll back Deal creation.

The checkbox may be implemented as a placeholder now or completed by the Commercial Terms epic.

## Optional replacement section

Near the bottom:

* checkbox: **This Deal Replaces an Archived Deal**
* Archived Deal lookup shown/required only when checked.
* After new Deal creation, update the canonical old Deal `Superseded_By__c` relationship.
* Do not persist redundant forward/reverse lookups unless a reporting requirement later justifies both.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New Deal is created as Draft.
2. Operator/Partner cannot be created from their lookup controls.
3. Market State is optional.
4. Currency and Effective Start defaults behave as defined.
5. Source and Partner remain independent.
6. Replacement lookup is required only when replacement checkbox is selected and only returns Archived Deals.
7. Add Commercial Terms runs only after successful Deal commit and cannot roll back Deal creation.

fields.description:
## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Define Closed as a longer-term operational stop that reuses the Archived locked-state restrictions where practical, but keeps the Deal reactivatable and keeps its makeup reserved.

## Enter Closed

Through a controlled Close Deal action:

* show confirmation;
* Status → Closed;
* stamp Closed Date + Effective End Date through shared lifecycle tracking;
* keep raw Makeup Key reserved;
* apply the common locked-state business-field restrictions used by Archived where practical;
* mark all currently Active Affiliate Links inactive;
* queue the resulting Deal snapshot to CMS;
* do not alter DRAs.

**Confirmation copy:**

> Closing this Deal will lock it and mark all currently active Affiliate Links inactive in Salesforce. The changes will be queued to the CMS. Reactivating the Deal will not automatically reactivate its Affiliate Links.

## Reactivate from Closed

* Show Reactivate only to permitted users using practical Permission Set/action visibility.
* Status → Active.
* Shared lifecycle logic clears Effective End Date.
* Makeup remains the same Deal/External Deal ID.
* Affiliate Links remain inactive in V1; do not restore the pre-close active set automatically.
* Do not alter DRAs.
* Queue CMS sync.

## Closed vs Archived

Shared:

* normal business fields locked;
* system/integration/audit fields may still update;
* end-state date behavior;
* active Links are shut off.

Different:

* Closed keeps makeup reserved.
* Closed can Reactivate.
* Archived releases makeup and never uses normal Reactivate.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Close locks normal business editing but preserves system/integration updates.
2. Close stamps Closed Date + Effective End Date.
3. Active Links become inactive; already inactive Links stay inactive.
4. Close does not change DRAs.
5. Closed keeps the raw Makeup Key reserved.
6. Closed → Active clears Effective End Date.
7. Closed → Active does not automatically reactivate Affiliate Links in V1.
8. Archived has no Reactivate action.

fields.description:
## Purpose

Capture the explicit follow-up for tomorrow's WagerTech review: decide whether Affiliate Links need their own terminal **Archived** state rather than relying only on Active/Inactive + Exclude from CMS.

## Current interim behavior

Until this decision changes it:

* Deal Pause deactivates currently Active Links and may restore the pre-pause active set.
* Deal Close deactivates currently Active Links; Closed → Active leaves them inactive.
* Deal Archive deactivates currently Active Links.
* Deal Inactive does not change Links.
* Previously-published Links remain in the full current eligible snapshot until CMS omission semantics are confirmed.

## If Link Archived is adopted, reconcile as one coordinated workstream

* Link data model / status values;
* Link manager create/edit/end-of-life UX;
* Deal Close and Deal Archive behavior;
* WAGR-456 payload eligibility and serialized status/state;
* WAGR-491 Exclude/Delete rules;
* CMS omission semantics / tombstone expectations;
* WAGR-459 staging tests;
* migration/backfill of existing inactive Links;
* reporting/history/SLC attribution.

## Questions for WagerTech / Strah

1. Is Archived terminal for a Link?
2. Should Deal Archive move all child Links to Archived rather than Inactive?
3. Should Deal Close archive Links, or only deactivate them?
4. Should Archived Links remain in future payloads?
5. If omitted, does CMS retain the last-known state?
6. Can an Archived Link ever be restored, or must a new Link be created?

## Done when

Decision is recorded in Confluence and the affected Jira stories are updated together. Do not implement Link Archived piecemeal before this review.
